sections.title: Overview
blocks: A multisystem **granulomatous** disease of unknown cause, with **non-caseating epithelioid granulomas**. It affects lungs/mediastinal nodes (~90%), skin (~25–35%), eyes (~25%), liver, heart, nerves, kidneys and bones. Peak onset 25–45 years; commoner in Afro-Caribbean and Scandinavian people.

ul: **Löfgren syndrome:** acute sarcoidosis with **erythema nodosum + bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (BHL)** ± fever and **ankle periarthritis**. It has a **good prognosis (>80–90% resolve within 2 years)**.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: An exaggerated Th1/Th17 response to an unidentified antigen (mycobacterial/propionibacterial antigens, environmental dusts are proposed) in genetically susceptible people (HLA-DRB1*03 linked with Löfgren). It forms granulomas.

ul: **Hypercalcaemia:** granuloma macrophages express **1-α-hydroxylase** → convert 25-OH vitamin D to **calcitriol** independently of PTH → ↑ gut calcium absorption. Worse with sun or vitamin D supplements.
**Anaemia:** chronic disease, marrow/splenic involvement.
**EN** is a reactive (non-specific) septal panniculitis, **not a granuloma**. "Specific" lesions (papules, plaques, lupus pernio, scar sarcoid) contain granulomas.
**Rash:** **bilateral tender, warm, red-violaceous, ill-defined nodules/plaques on the shins** (EN, photo G01), with fever, malaise and arthralgia.

**How an EN nodule evolves clinically**: bright red, raised, tender nodule → flattens and turns **dusky violaceous/blue** → **yellow-green bruise-like** colour ("erythema contusiformis") over 1–2 weeks → fades **without ulceration, atrophy or scarring** in **3–6 weeks**; new crops may appear.

**Specific cutaneous sarcoid:** **red-brown papules/plaques** (face, lips, nose — "**apple-jelly**" on diascopy, G05); **lupus pernio** (violaceous nose/cheeks/ears — chronic disease, upper-airway/lung fibrosis, bone cysts; G03); **scar/tattoo sarcoid**; subcutaneous (Darier–Roussy) nodules; annular, hypopigmented, ichthyosiform, ulcerative forms; scarring alopecia; nail dystrophy

**Systemic:** cough, breathlessness, chest pain; uveitis (red/painful eye, blurred vision — can be asymptomatic); parotid enlargement; facial palsy (Heerfordt); arrhythmia/heart block (cardiac sarcoid — sudden death); hepatosplenomegaly; renal stones; fatigue (very common).
**The case:** breathlessness, **weight loss 3 kg, night sweats**, EN, **anaemia (Hb 10.8)**, **calcium 2.7 mmol/L**, CXR showing **BHL**.
**CXR: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy** ± right paratracheal nodes and parenchymal changes. Scadding stages: 0 normal; **I BHL only**; II BHL + infiltrates; III infiltrates only; IV fibrosis.

**Diagnosis: acute sarcoidosis, Löfgren-type** (EN + BHL; hypercalcaemia supports sarcoid): BUT **weight loss + night sweats + anaemia** mean **TB and lymphoma must be excluded** — both cause BHL, systemic symptoms and EN

**Investigations (BTS clinical statement 2021 / ERS):** **TB:** IGRA, sputum AFB/culture, HIV test; **Bloods:** FBC + film, LDH (lymphoma), **calcium (adjusted) + 24-h urine calcium**, U&E/eGFR, LFT, **serum ACE** (supportive only — low sensitivity and specificity; **ACE inhibitors lower it**, so interpret with the drug history), vitamin D (25-OH and 1,25-OH), immunoglobulins; **Lungs:** **HRCT chest**; **PFTs with TLCO**; **ECG for all** (heart block) ± Holter, echo, cardiac MRI if symptomatic or abnormal ECG; **Ophthalmology review for all** (uveitis); **Tissue:** **EBUS-TBNA** of mediastinal nodes or biopsy of a **specific skin lesion** (non-caseating granulomas; stain and culture for AFB/fungi). In a **classic Löfgren presentation** without atypical features, tissue confirmation can be omitted — **not here**, given the B symptoms; Urinalysis

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: **TB** (caseating granulomas, IGRA), **lymphoma** (B symptoms, high LDH, nodes elsewhere), metastatic cancer, histoplasmosis/fungal infection, **berylliosis** (occupational), hypersensitivity pneumonitis, drug-induced sarcoid-like reactions (**checkpoint inhibitors, TNF inhibitors, interferon**), granulomatosis with polyangiitis, IgG4 disease. Skin: granuloma annulare, lupus vulgaris (cutaneous TB), leishmaniasis, foreign-body granulomas, lupus, rosacea, lymphoma. **EN differentials**: see the [drug eruption](condition:drug-eruption-approach) notes see *Eruptive xanthomas — new diabetes* (cellulitis, thrombophlebitis/DVT, erythema induratum, other panniculitis, cutaneous PAN, insect bites, Sweet syndrome, bruising).

sections.title: Management

ul: **Refer to respiratory (sarcoid clinic). Admit** if hypoxic, unwell, severe hypercalcaemia (≥3.0 mmol/L or symptomatic), cardiac or neurological involvement.
**Löfgren syndrome:** usually self-limiting — **NSAIDs** for EN/arthralgia (if renal function/GI risk allow), rest, leg elevation. A **short oral corticosteroid course** if severe.

**Hypercalcaemia:** hydration; **stop vitamin D/calcium supplements**; avoid excess sun; review thiazides (raise calcium) and lithium; glucocorticoids treat sarcoid hypercalcaemia (specialist); monitor U&E (nephrocalcinosis/stones)

**Systemic/organ-threatening sarcoid (specialist; ERS 2021):** prednisolone (e.g. 20–40 mg/day, tapering), methotrexate (steroid-sparing), azathioprine/leflunomide/mycophenolate, **infliximab/adalimumab** for refractory disease and lupus pernio.

**Cutaneous sarcoid:** potent/very potent TCS or **intralesional triamcinolone**, **hydroxychloroquine**, **doxycycline/minocycline**, methotrexate; TNF inhibitors for disfiguring lupus pernio; JAK inhibitors (emerging, off-label). Camouflage.

**Pharmacist checklist:** steroid card, bone protection (**caution with vitamin D/calcium supplements in hypercalcaemic sarcoid** — specialist advice), PJP prophylaxis if heavily immunosuppressed, vaccines (inactivated), TB screening before TNF inhibitors, MTX safety, HCQ eye screening, ECG awareness (QT, conduction).

blocks: Recognition, bloods (calcium, U&E, LFT), CXR request (where the IP has rights), NSAID analgesia, stopping vitamin D/calcium supplements, referral, and long-term medicines support. Specialist diagnosis and immunosuppression.

refer.t: Palpitations, syncope or heart block: possible **cardiac sarcoid**, urgent assessment.
Red painful eye or blurred vision: same-day ophthalmology (uveitis).

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Palpitations, syncope or heart block: possible **cardiac sarcoid**, urgent assessment.
Red painful eye or blurred vision: same-day ophthalmology (uveitis).

blocks: Hypercalcaemia (thirst, polyuria, confusion), palpitations/syncope/heart block (cardiac sarcoid — urgent), visual symptoms/red eye (same-day ophthalmology), facial palsy/neurology, worsening breathlessness/hypoxia, B symptoms suggesting lymphoma/TB, lupus pernio (chronic disease).

pearls: "**EN + BHL = Löfgren — but B symptoms or anaemia mean exclude TB and lymphoma.**"
In patients with sarcoid, **check before recommending OTC vitamin D or calcium**.
Every patient with sarcoid needs an **eye check and an ECG**.
